name: Driving schools

problems.words: Students cancel at the last minute and instructors sit idle
quick_ideas: Agree a cancellation rule and tell students when they book, so it's clear upfront
Remind students the day before, so they cancel earlier or turn up.

workzap_build.text: lesson booking with automatic reminders and the cancellation rule recorded on each booking.

problems.ask_first: Is there any rule students agree to about cancelling today?
problems.free_stops: Reminder timing and the rule set-up are in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count last week's cancelled lessons by instructor and time of day, so you can see when idle car time hits hardest.
Have each instructor mark tomorrow's lesson confirmations in one shared notebook by evening, so empty slots can be reassigned sooner.

problems.words: Double bookings on the same car and instructor
quick_ideas: Keep one booking diary for all cars and instructors, so every booking is checked
Let one person confirm bookings, so clashes are caught.

workzap_build.text: a lesson calendar by instructor and car that blocks double bookings, with WhatsApp self-booking.

problems.ask_first: Do double bookings come mostly at weekends, or on busy weekday evenings?
problems.free_stops: Calendar rules are in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Note every booking clash this week with the car and instructor involved, so you can spot where double booking starts.
Assign one person to write every confirmed lesson in one master diary, so car and instructor clashes get checked before promises are made.

problems.words: I don't know how many lessons each instructor gave
quick_ideas: Log every lesson with start and end time, so lessons can be counted
Total each instructor's lessons weekly, so pay and workload are clear.

workzap_build.text: an instructor lesson log confirmed by the student, feeding pay or commission automatically.

problems.ask_first: Are instructors' lessons noted anywhere today, or only remembered at pay time?
problems.free_stops: How confirmation and pay calculations work is in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare each instructor's completed lesson slips for this week, so workload differences stop being guessed.
Make each instructor hand in one daily lesson tally to one owner notebook, so weekly counts are ready without chasing.

problems.words: We don't track how many lessons each student has left
quick_ideas: Keep a package card per student showing lessons bought and taken, so both sides know
Update it after every lesson, so refunds are clear.

workzap_build.text: a package tracker showing lessons bought, taken and remaining, with payment status, holding no personal details beyond what's needed.

problems.ask_first: Do students ask about lessons left mostly mid-course, or only when they want a refund?
problems.free_stops: Package tracking set-up is in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count how many active students have no clear lessons remaining noted today, so you see how big the tracking mess is.
Give one staff member one notebook page per active learner package, so remaining lessons stay clear before new bookings are promised.

quick_ideas: List students with unpaid balances, so you know the gap
Remind each once, so it's raised early.

workzap_build.text: payment status per package with automatic reminders.

problems.ask_first: Do students leave mostly after the first payment, or in the middle of the course?
problems.free_stops: Reminder steps are in the solution document; refund obligations are for your lawyer.

extra_ideas.text: Count part paid students who have no next lesson written in the diary, so stuck cash is clearer this week.
Keep one unpaid balance notebook at the front desk with one staff owner, so follow ups happen before lessons drift away.

problems.words: Enquiries on Instagram and WhatsApp get late replies
quick_ideas: Give one person the job of replying at set times, so enquiries aren't left
Note where each enquiry came from, so you see which channel works.

workzap_build.text: an enquiry inbox from Instagram, WhatsApp and website with response tracking and source.

problems.ask_first: Which channel gets the late replies: Instagram, WhatsApp, or both?
problems.free_stops: Inbox and source set-up are in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Note the time each enquiry arrives and the time it gets answered today, so slow reply periods stand out clearly.
Give one person fixed reply windows and one handwritten enquiry list, so messages stop sitting unseen during busy lesson hours.

problems.words: Instructors teach differently and students get confused
quick_ideas: Agree the skills a course covers in order, so instructors share one plan
Note what each lesson covered, so the next instructor picks up from there.

workzap_build.text: a progress card per student listing skills covered, shared between instructors.

problems.ask_first: Do students get confused mostly about the same lessons, or across the whole course?
problems.free_stops: The progress card structure is in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Listen for which lesson topics students mention as repeated or skipped this week, so confusing differences between instructors become visible.
Make every instructor leave a short handover note after each lesson in one place, so the next lesson follows the same learning path.

problems.words: Fuel and repairs on training cars keep rising
quick_ideas: Record each fill and repair per car, so costs are visible by car
Compare cars of the same type, so outliers show.

workzap_build.text: a car log for fuel, kilometres, damage and service schedule.

problems.ask_first: Do costs rise mostly from fuel, or from repairs on a few older cars?
problems.free_stops: How the log is kept is in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare each training car's fuel notes with the lessons it actually ran this week, so the thirstiest routine shows.
Let one person collect all fuel slips and repair notes in one car folder daily, so repeat costs stop slipping past review.

problems.words: Weekend and evening slots are full, weekday mornings empty
quick_ideas: Look at last month's bookings by time slot, so you see the empty hours
Offer quiet slots to students with flexible schedules, so they fill.

workzap_build.text: a utilisation view of empty slots, with offers sent to students who have agreed to messages.

problems.ask_first: Are mornings empty on every weekday, or only on certain days?
problems.free_stops: How offers are targeted is in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count booked and empty lesson slots this week by morning, evening and weekend, so the quiet times are clear to everyone.
Let one staff member review next week's empty weekday morning slots at a fixed time, so they can match flexible learners earlier.

never_say: How to pass tests, bypass test steps, or get a licence improperly; decline fake certificates, bribes or proxy test-takers.
Advice on licensing rules, instructor certification or insurance.
Storing students' names, phone numbers or personal details beyond what the owner needs.
Judging harassment or misconduct complaints; if anyone is in danger, point to police or emergency services.
Whether a refund is legally owed.
After a lesson crash with injuries, anything before pointing to emergency services.

sample_reply.person: Students book on WhatsApp and cancel an hour before. My instructors sit doing nothing. Any solution?
sample_reply.pi: Yes, there's a fix for this, and you can start this week. 1) Agree a cancellation rule and tell students when they book, so it's clear upfront. 2) Remind students the day before, so they cancel earlier or turn up. Workzap can do this automatically for you: lesson booking with reminders and your cancellation rule recorded on each booking. Shall I get a solution document and quote prepared for you? You're free to say no.
